title: Scalar extension of a finite free coefficient-module sheaf with its standard basis
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], R and S sheaves of commutative rings, a:R -> S, U a site object, and I a finite index type. The sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] of the free R|U-module with basis I is isomorphic to the free S|U-module with that basis [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There is such an isomorphism which sends the sheafification-unit image of 1 tensor each standard integral basis section to the corresponding standard rational basis section on every test object over U. Empty objects, zero rings and empty I are allowed.

proof.text: Identify sections of each free finite sheaf with the finite product of the section ring, using freeSectionsLinearEquiv. Transport the tensor source along that equivalence, commute tensor product with the finite product by TensorProduct.piRight, use S tensor_R R = S in each coordinate by AlgebraTensorModule.rid, and transport back to the sections of the target free sheaf. These are explicit linear equivalences, not witnesses chosen from an unproved existence assertion.

proof.text: The coordinate formula sends b tensor m to the vector whose ith entry is b times a applied to the ith coordinate of m. On pure tensors 1 tensor m, naturality of the free coordinate projections and of the coefficient map proves that this formula commutes with restriction. Pure tensors generate, so the sectionwise linear equivalences define a presheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), proof, pp. 59--60, scalar extension of the standard finite free integral module

proof.text: Sheafify the presheaf isomorphism. Its target is already the free S-module sheaf, so the sheafification adjunction counit identifies its sheafification with itself. Naturality of the unit followed by the adjunction triangle identifies the composite on each original tensor section with the sectionwise coordinate formula.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), proof, pp. 59--60, scalar extension of the standard finite free integral module

proof.text: Apply the formula to each standard basis section. The free basis inclusions and projections satisfy the Kronecker-delta identities, and the coefficient map preserves zero and one. The image therefore has exactly the coordinates of the corresponding target basis section. Injectivity of the target coordinate equivalence proves the required normalization. No point is chosen and no nonzero basis index is assumed to exist, so the empty and rank-zero cases are included.
